concepts.name: Generative AI
concepts.brief_description: AI that creates new content (text, images, music, code) by learning patterns from data, mimicking human creativity.

concepts.name: Foundation Models
concepts.brief_description: Large-scale, generalized AI models trained on massive datasets; they can perform multiple tasks unlike specialized models.

concepts.name: Transformer Architecture
concepts.brief_description: Neural network architecture based on self-attention that serves as the backbone for modern foundation models.

concepts.name: Pre-training
concepts.brief_description: Process of training foundation models on large, diverse datasets to learn general capabilities before specialization.

concepts.name: Fine-tuning
concepts.brief_description: Adapting a pre-trained model to a specific task or domain by further training on targeted data.

concepts.name: Prompt Engineering
concepts.brief_description: Crafting input prompts to guide generative models toward desired outputs, improving response quality.

concepts.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
concepts.brief_description: Combining generative models with external data retrieval to produce answers grounded in up-to-date or private information.

concepts.name: AI Agents
concepts.brief_description: Software systems that use LLMs and tools to perceive, reason, and act autonomously to accomplish tasks for users.

concepts.name: Evaluation Metrics
concepts.brief_description: Quantitative measures (e.g., accuracy, BLEU, human preference) used to assess generative model performance.

concepts.name: Deployment
concepts.brief_description: Process of making trained generative models accessible via APIs, services, or integrated into applications.

concepts.name: Machine Learning
concepts.brief_description: Statistical approach where models learn patterns from data to make predictions or classifications.

concepts.name: Deep Learning
concepts.brief_description: Subset of machine learning using deep neural networks, especially transformers, to model complex patterns.

concepts.name: Curriculum Design
concepts.brief_description: Structured learning path covering both builder (model creation) and user (application) perspectives of generative AI.

concepts.name: Technology Success Criteria
concepts.brief_description: Four criteria for a technology to be considered successful: solves real-world problems, useful daily, creates economic impact, generates new jobs, and is accessible.

key_phrases: Generative AI creates new content by learning patterns from data
Foundation models are generalized, large-scale AI models
Transformer architecture is the backbone of modern generative AI
Pre-training and fine-tuning pipeline for foundation models
Prompt engineering improves LLM output quality
RAG combines generative models with external data retrieval
AI agents use LLMs and tools to perform autonomous tasks
Successful technology must solve real-world problems daily
Builder perspective focuses on building and deploying models
User perspective focuses on applying models through APIs and tools
